text: deploy/examples/atproto/market/accept.sh is the live acceptance of this example: it brings the whole market up in a throwaway state directory and exits non-zero unless every workload is up and reachable. It is bash with set -euo pipefail; ACCEPT_ROOT (default a fresh mktemp -d) is the one directory it owns, and an EXIT trap stops everything it started and removes that directory. It never stops or touches a kcp, kine or OpenBao it did not start. It asks the kernel for three free 127.0.0.1 ports, for kcp, kine and OpenBao, instead of pinning any, so it cannot collide with another instance on the machine. It starts kcp with ROOT=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp and KCP_SECURE_PORT and KINE_ENDPOINT set to two of those ports through deploy/start-kcp.sh; installs the provider with KUBECONFIG_PATH=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp/admin.kubeconfig through deploy/install-provider.sh; builds ./cmd/deno-kcp-provider into $ACCEPT_ROOT; starts OpenBao with OPENBAO_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/openbao and OPENBAO_LISTEN on the third port through deploy/start-openbao.sh; and runs the provider with --kubeconfig, --openbao-addr http://<openbao port>, --openbao-token root and RUNS_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/runs. It then runs deploy/examples/atproto/market/apply.sh with ORG_ROOT the repository parent, KUBECONFIG the kcp admin kubeconfig, OPENBAO_LISTEN the same address, START_OPENBAO=0, a bounded WAIT_SECONDS, and KEY_FILE, BOB_KEY_FILE and BIDDER_KEY_FILE under $ACCEPT_ROOT. When apply.sh returns, whether it succeeded or not, accept.sh reads every DenoPod from kcp with kubectl and prints one line per check, each with its result and the decisive evidence: apply.sh exited 0; DenoPod plc in root:global, relay in root:relay, pds in root:alice, pds in root:bob and bidder in root:bob each reached phase Running and report ready true; DenoPod verifier in root:alice reached the terminal phase Succeeded; bob pds answers on its own name, which the provider proves with its readiness probe through the shim (kcpdns pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /xrpc/_health) and the host proves by fetching the same path from outside with curl https://127.0.0.1:2585/xrpc/_health; the bidder answers on bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /oauth-client-metadata.json and on https://127.0.0.1:2586/oauth-client-metadata.json. Both host checks use https, because every service pod sets SERVICE_TLS true and the provider issues it a leaf, so the listener the host reaches is the TLS one; an http:// fetch of a TLS listener is not a check of anything and must not be written. http_code reports the status curl printed, and prints 000 exactly once when the fetch failed rather than appending a second fallback. And the five long-running pods are still Running with ready true when they are read a second time at least ten seconds later, so a pod that dies after startup fails the run. It prints a final table naming every check and its result, prints the tail of the provider log and the status of the failing pod when a check fails, and exits 0 only when every check passed.

text: restartChildProcess takes the child-process lock for its whole body and switches on AgentConfig.Exec.RestartOnSecretChanges: "always" stops the running child process after marking the state childProcessStateRestarting, "never" returns nil without restarting when the process is running, and any other value returns an error of the form invalid value for restart-on-secret-changes with the quoted value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: restartChildProcess prepares the command with child.CommandPrep and returns a wrapped error when parsing fails, then builds a child.NewInput that wires os.Stdin, os.Stdout and os.Stderr, sets Timeout to 0 so the process runs forever, sets Env to os.Environ() plus the newly rendered variables, leaves ReloadSignal nil because reloading cannot change environment variables, uses AgentConfig.Exec.RestartStopSignal as KillSignal and a 30-second KillTimeout, and sets Setpgid from the subshell flag returned by CommandPrep. After child.New and Start it records the process and sets childProcessState to childProcessStateRunning, returning a wrapped error if Start fails.

text: On each TemplateRenderedCh event Server.Run reads the runner render events and proceeds only when the event count reaches numberOfTemplates and no event has a zero LastWouldRender, so an incomplete render batch is skipped. label: SpecRequirement
text: When an exit code arrives on childProcessExitCh because the child process exited on its own, Server.Run returns a *ProcessExitError carrying that code.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: After a successful child Start, restartChildProcess starts a goroutine that reads proc.ExitCh() and forwards a received exit code onto childProcessExitCh so the main Run loop can surface it as a ProcessExitError; the read must happen after Start to avoid racing with ExitCh initialization.

text: NewServer copies cfg.Logger into the server logger, retains cfg as the server config, sets childProcessState to childProcessStateNotStarted, allocates an unbuffered childProcessExitCh channel, and returns a pointer to the server so Run can be invoked on it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ServerConfig carries the hclog.Logger and *config.Config agent configuration plus the Namespace, LogLevel and LogWriter settings; LogLevel and LogWriter exist so the internal consul-template runner's own logger matches the agent's log level and writes to the same io.Writer, since that logger cannot be set or copied externally.

label: SpecRequirement
text: run serves HTTP on the address ":" plus the port flag, with read, write and idle timeouts of 20 seconds each; the handler encodes a fresh Response of the current environment and PID as JSON with status 200 and Content-Type application/json, honoring a query parameter pretty=1 by indenting the output with two spaces.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Configuration is parsed by the standard flag package in init, with no environment variables backing any option: --port (uint, default 34000) sets the HTTP listen port; --sleep-after-stop-signal (duration, default 1s) sets the pause after a stop signal; --use-sigusr1 (bool, default false) selects SIGUSR1 instead of SIGTERM as the stop signal; --stop-after (duration, default 0) stops the process after that duration; --exit-code (int, default 0) sets the code returned at exit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Response struct carries the process environment as a map of variable name to value under the JSON key environment_variables and the current process identifier under the JSON key process_id.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The process stops on whichever comes first: a 60 second context timeout, the configured stop signal, or the --stop-after duration elapsing; on a stop signal it sleeps for --sleep-after-stop-signal when that value is positive before continuing.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: When secretIDFilePath is set, Authenticate stats and reads that file, trims the value into cachedSecretID, and on read error or empty content fails with the matching "... secret ID ..." error unless a cached secret ID is already known, in which case it logs a warning and reuses the cached value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Lease keys are produced by autoIncrementedLeaseKey from the lease bucket's NextSequence, encoded as uint64 big endian into an 8 byte key and paired with an entry in the lookup bucket mapping the caller's id to that key, so that byte-slice ordering of keys preserves creation order and parents are restored before children.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Clear wipes the store by deleting the token, lease and lookup buckets inside one Update transaction, emitting a trace log "deleting bolt bucket" per bucket, and then re-runs createBoltSchema at the current storage version so the empty schema is restored.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewBoltStorage runs createBoltSchema inside a single Update transaction at storage version "2"; createBoltSchema rejects any other version with "schema version %s not supported", creates the version-2 buckets token, lease and lookup, ensures the meta bucket exists, writes the version key into meta when absent, and is a no-op when the stored version already equals the requested version.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DBFileExists reports whether the cache file exists by attempting os.OpenFile on filepath.Join(path, DatabaseFileName) with the O_RDWR flag and mode 0600; a successful open closes the file and returns true with the close error, os.IsNotExist returns false, nil, and any other error is wrapped as "failed to check if bolt file exists at path %s: %w".

label: SpecRequirement
text: GetByType reads the named bucket in a View transaction, decrypts every stored blob with the wrapper and AAD, and returns the plaintext values in iteration order; decryption failures do not abort the scan but are collected into a multierror returned alongside whatever decrypted successfully, and a missing bucket fails with "bucket %q not found".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Close emits a trace log "closing bolt db" carrying the database path and then closes the underlying bolt.DB.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every cached payload is stored as an encrypted wrapping.BlobInfo protobuf, encrypted and decrypted through the configured wrapping.Wrapper with the configured AAD; the only values kept in cleartext are the schema version key and the retrieval-token material.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Retrieval-token material is stored unencrypted in the meta bucket under the RetrievalTokenMaterial key: StoreRetrievalToken puts the raw bytes there in an Update transaction, and GetRetrievalToken copies them out of a View transaction and returns nil when the key is unset; both fail with "bucket %q not found" when the meta bucket is missing.

label: SpecInterface
name: BoltStorage.GetByType
signature: func (b *BoltStorage) GetByType(ctx context.Context, indexType string) ([][]byte, error)

label: SpecRequirement
text: When the stored version is "1" and the requested version is "2", createBoltSchema migrates in place: it creates the v2 schema, moves every entry of the deprecated auth-lease and secret-lease buckets into the lease bucket under a freshly generated auto-increment key, records the id-to-key mapping in the lookup bucket, deletes the deprecated buckets, and rewrites the meta version key to "2"; any other stored-to-requested version pair fails with "storage migration from %s to %s not implemented".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Delete removes an entry by id: for the lease type it first resolves the id through the lookup bucket, failing with "failed to lookup bolt DB key for id %q" when absent, deletes the lookup entry, then deletes the resolved key from the target bucket; for other types the id is used directly as the key; a missing bucket fails with "bucket %q not found during delete" and a successful delete emits a trace log "deleted index from bolt db".

label: SpecRequirement
text: The database lives at filepath.Join(config.Path, DatabaseFileName) where DatabaseFileName is the constant "vault-agent-cache.db"; NewBoltStorage opens it with mode 0600 and a 1 second bolt open timeout, and the joined path is the only file the storage touches.

label: SpecRequirement
text: GetAutoAuthToken reads the AutoAuthToken key from the meta bucket, copies the ciphertext out of the transaction, returns nil, nil when the value is absent, and otherwise decrypts it, returning "failed to decrypt auto-auth token: %w" on decryption failure; a missing meta bucket fails with "bucket %q not found".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Set encrypts the plaintext with b.wrapper.Encrypt(ctx, plaintext, wrapping.WithAad([]byte(b.aad))) and stores the protobuf-marshalled wrapping.BlobInfo; it accepts only indexType lease, which stores under a new auto-increment key, or indexType token, which stores under the id key and also writes the same blob into the meta bucket under the AutoAuthToken key; any other type fails with "called Set for unsupported type %q" and a missing bucket fails with "bucket %q not found".

label: SpecRequirement
text: BoltStorageConfig supplies the cache directory Path, an hclog.Logger, a wrapping.Wrapper used to encrypt and decrypt entries, and an AAD string passed as associated data on every encrypt and decrypt call; NewBoltStorage copies Logger, Wrapper and AAD onto the returned BoltStorage and uses only Path to locate the database file.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The schema must define one table named `indexer` whose indexes are `id` (unique, StringFieldIndex on ID), `request_path` (non-unique, CompoundIndex over Namespace then RequestPath), `token` (unique, AllowMissing, on Token), `token_accessor` (unique, AllowMissing, on TokenAccessor), `lease` (unique, AllowMissing, on Lease), `lease_token` (non-unique, AllowMissing, on LeaseToken) and `token_parent` (non-unique, AllowMissing, on TokenParent).

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flush must build a fresh empty database and swap it into the CacheMemDB atomic pointer, leaving previously stored entries unreachable; a failure to build the replacement database must return the error and leave the existing database in place.

label: SpecRequirement
text: CacheMemDB must hold its memdb instance behind an atomic pointer so readers that load the database before a Flush continue on the old instance while later operations use the new one.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Set must reject a nil index with an error, insert the index into the `indexer` table in a write transaction, abort the transaction when the insert fails, and commit only on success.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Index must carry the lookup keys the schema indexes, the serialized Response bytes, the HTTP request shape (RequestMethod, RequestToken, RequestHeader) and LastRenewed, plus a Type string classifying the entry as token, auth-lease or secret-lease.

text: New must build a memdb database from the package schema, store it in the CacheMemDB atomic pointer, and return the CacheMemDB; a schema construction failure must surface as an error with no CacheMemDB returned.

text: GetByPrefix must validate the index name, append the `_prefix` suffix to derive the memdb prefix index, iterate all matching objects in a read-only transaction and collect them into a slice; a cast failure on any element must return an error and no partial result.

text: The package should keep its cache_memdb_test.go and index_test.go suites covering the store operations and the index serialization round trip, since these are the only checks on the memdb schema behavior.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PassthroughKeyManager must satisfy KeyManager, enforced at compile time by the assertion var _ KeyManager = (*PassthroughKeyManager)(nil); a change that removes either method from the type must break the build.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PassthroughKeyManager.Wrapper must return the manager's stored *aead.Wrapper unchanged, so callers perform key operations against the same wrapper the constructor configured.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package should keep passthrough_test.go exercising the passthrough constructor together with both Wrapper and RetrievalToken, so the key-size branches and the nil-wrapper error path stay covered.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package must expose a KeyManager interface whose contract is exactly two methods: Wrapper, which returns a wrapping.Wrapper usable for key-related operations, and RetrievalToken, which takes a context and returns the byte material that lets a caller source back the encryption key, where that material may be the encryption key itself or a token or identifier exchanged for it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewPassthroughKeyManager must build an aead wrapper, set its config with key_id mapped to KeyID, install the resolved root key bytes through SetAesGcmKeyBytes, and return a PassthroughKeyManager holding that wrapper; a failure from the random read, SetConfig or SetAesGcmKeyBytes must abort with a nil manager and the underlying error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PassthroughKeyManager.RetrievalToken must return the key bytes held by the wrapper, obtained through KeyBytes with the caller's context, and must return a nil token with the error "unable to get wrapper for token retrieval" when the wrapper is nil; because the manager is a passthrough it must not abstract, re-wrap or transform the key material before returning it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package must define the constant KeyID with the value "root" and use it as the key_id config entry when configuring a wrapper.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewPassthroughKeyManager must branch on the length of the supplied key: a zero-length key causes it to draw 32 fresh bytes from crypto/rand and use them as the root key, a 32-byte key is used verbatim, and any other length must return a nil manager with the error formatted as "invalid key size, should be 32, got %d" carrying the observed length.

text: SinkServer.Run rejects a nil incoming channel before starting its loop and returns the error "sink server: incoming channel is nil".

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: When writeSink returns an error, Run logs "error returned by sink function, retrying" with the error and the backoff, waits a randomized backoff drawn from 2 seconds plus ss.random until 2 seconds minus 1 second, that is in the range [1s, 3s), and re-enqueues the same sinkToken; a context cancellation during the wait stops the timer and returns nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewSinkServer copies Logger, Client and ExitAfterAuth from the SinkServerConfig into the SinkServer and seeds a math/rand source from time.Now().Nanosecond(); the remaining counter starts at zero and SinkServer's fields stay unexported.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The SinkReader interface declares exactly one method, Token() string, so a caller can read back the token a sink currently holds without depending on the destination type.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The per-sink write path checks that the token being written is still the latest token, then applies wrapping first and encryption second, and passes the resulting token to Sink.WriteToken; a token that has been superseded is skipped without error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SinkServerConfig carries the Logger, api Client, Context and ExitAfterAuth switch that NewSinkServer consumes; the context field is present in the config type even though Run takes its own ctx argument.

label: SpecRequirement
text: For a new token and a non-empty sink list, Run drains any pending work from the sink channel, records the token as latest, then enqueues one sinkToken per SinkConfig while incrementing the remaining atomic counter once per sink; each dequeued sinkToken is written and decrements the counter.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Run keeps the most recent token and ignores any incoming token equal to it, so a repeated token is not fanned out to the sinks again.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When a SinkConfig has a non-empty DHType, the token is encrypted before it reaches the sink: for curve25519 the remote public key is read from DHPath and decoded once and cached, a local key pair is generated once and cached, the shared secret is computed from the cached private and remote public keys, DeriveKey selects dhutil.DeriveSharedKey over the raw secret, an empty AES key is an error, and the token is sealed with EncryptAES using AAD and emitted as an encoded JSON envelope carrying the local public key, nonce and encrypted payload.

label: SpecRequirement
text: fileSink.WriteToken must generate a UUID, open a temporary file named "<basename>.tmp.<first UUID segment>" in the same directory as the configured path with the sink's mode, and write either the supplied token or, when the token is empty, the UUID itself; when writing fails it must close and remove the temporary file, ignoring those errors, and return a wrapped error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package tests must cover sink construction against a real temporary path, the mode override on the written file, and the uid/gid chown override, and must also contain a sink test file for the surrounding sink behaviour.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewFileSink must reject a nil logger with the error "nil logger provided", reject a config map with no "path" key with "'path' not specified for file sink", and reject a non-string path value with "could not parse 'path' as string"; on success it returns a fileSink implementing sink.Sink.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewFileSink must call WriteToken with the empty string before returning the sink, so construction verifies the target directory is writable, and must wrap any failure as "error during write check"; a successful check must leave no file behind.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewFileSink must default the file mode to 0o640 and set uid and gid to -1, meaning ownership is left unchanged, when the corresponding Config keys are absent.

label: SpecRequirement
text: fileSink.WriteToken should return wrapped errors that name the failing step and path: UUID generation, temp file opening in the target directory, writing, closing, removing during the write check, changing ownership, and renaming to the target path, and should log a trace on entry and exit plus an info line when the token is written.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewFileSink must accept optional "mode", "uid" and "gid" integer overrides, erroring with "could not parse 'mode' as integer", "could not parse 'uid' as integer" or "could not parse 'gid' as integer" on a type mismatch, and erroring with "file mode does not represent a regular file" when the mode is not a regular file mode; the accepted values override the sink's stored mode, uid and gid.

label: SpecRequirement
text: On an empty token fileSink.WriteToken must treat the call as a write check, removing the temporary file and returning nil; on a non-empty token it must apply the configured uid and gid through os.Chown only when either differs from -1, then rename the temporary file over the configured path so the token lands atomically.

label: SpecRequirement
text: inmemSink.WriteToken must store the given token in the sink's atomic token value, and then, when a lease cache is present, call the cache's RegisterAutoAuthToken with that token and return the resulting error. When no lease cache is present the method must return nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: New must accept a *sink.SinkConfig and a *cache.LeaseCache and return a value satisfying sink.Sink together with a nil error, retaining the lease cache so that later token writes can register with it. A nil lease cache must still produce a usable sink.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: Execute loops reading change requests from the request channel and dispatches on the command field, so the service stays alive and responsive until a stop or shutdown command ends it.

text: EncryptAES takes a symmetric key, a plaintext and associated data, and returns the ciphertext and the nonce used for it, with an error on failure, so the caller can transmit both outputs.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecInterface
name: DecryptAES
signature: func DecryptAES(key, ciphertext, nonce, aad []byte) ([]byte, error)

label: SpecRequirement
text: GeneratePublicPrivateKey reads 32 random bytes from crypto/rand into a scalar, computes the Curve25519 public key with ScalarBaseMult, and returns the public key first and the private scalar second, together with any read error.

label: SpecInterface
name: Envelope
signature: type Envelope struct { Curve25519PublicKey []byte `json:"curve25519_public_key"`; Nonce []byte `json:"nonce"`; EncryptedPayload []byte `json:"encrypted_payload"` }

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: DeriveSharedKey returns exactly a 32-byte key, and returns no key at all when the HKDF read fails or reads a short value, so a caller never receives a partial key alongside an error.

label: SpecRequirement

label: SpecRequirement
text: PublicKeyInfo serializes its key as the JSON field curve25519_public_key, and Envelope serializes its public key, nonce and ciphertext as curve25519_public_key, nonce and encrypted_payload, so the on-the-wire field names stay stable across peers.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DecryptAES takes the symmetric key, the ciphertext, the nonce and the associated data and returns the recovered plaintext or an error, so a decryption under the wrong key, nonce or associated data fails rather than returning data.

label: SpecRequirement
text: JobManager.Start must run its body at most once via sync.Once, starting the dispatcher's workers and the background assignWork scheduling loop; a manager that has been stopped must not be restartable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Queue selection must proceed in round-robin order starting after lastQueueAccessed, skipping any queue whose tracked worker count is already at or above ceil(0.9 * numWorkers / numberOfActiveQueues), and it must record the chosen queue index in lastQueueAccessed; when every queue is saturated no job is handed out.

label: SpecInterface
name: JobManager
signature: type JobManager struct { name string; queues map[string]*list.List; quit chan struct{}; newWork chan struct{}; workerPool *dispatcher; workerCount map[string]int; onceStart sync.Once; onceStop sync.Once; logger log.Logger; totalJobs int; metricSink *metricsutil.ClusterMetricSink; wg sync.WaitGroup; l sync.RWMutex; queuesIndex []string; lastQueueAccessed int }

label: SpecRequirement
text: JobManager must expose read-locked accessors: GetPendingJobCount returns the sum of all queue lengths, GetWorkerCounts returns the queue-id to active-worker map, and GetWorkQueueLengths returns a fresh map of queue-id to queue length so callers cannot mutate internal state.

label: SpecInterface
name: NewJobManager
signature: func NewJobManager(name string, numWorkers int, l log.Logger, metricSink *metricsutil.ClusterMetricSink) *JobManager

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewJobManager must accept a name, a worker count, a logger and a metric sink; when the logger is nil it substitutes a Vault logger writing to io.Discard at NoLevel, when the name is empty it generates a uuid-based name of the form jobmanager-<guid> (falling back to the literal no-uuid when uuid generation fails and logging a warning), and it must create the backing dispatcher named <name>-dispatcher with the given worker count.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Dispatcher construction must coerce a worker count of zero or less to one and log a warning, substitute a discarding Vault logger for a nil logger, and generate a uuid-based dispatcher-<guid> name when the name is empty.

label: SpecRequirement
text: AddJob must take the write lock, create the queue for queueID together with its zeroed worker count when the queue does not yet exist, push the job onto the back of that queue, increment the total job counter, and, when a metric sink is configured, set the queue_length gauge labelled with queue_id and the total_jobs gauge; when the manager had no queues at all it must also non-blockingly signal the buffered newWork channel so work added before Start is not lost.

label: SpecInterface
name: Job
signature: type Job interface { Execute() error; OnFailure(err error) }

label: SpecRequirement
text: JobManager.Stop must run its body at most once via sync.Once, close the quit channel, wait on the waitgroup that tracks the scheduling loop, and then stop the worker pool so all workers exit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The scheduling loop must run in its own goroutine, repeatedly call getNextJob to pop the front job of the next eligible queue, dispatch it with callbacks that increment then decrement that queue's worker count, break out when no queue is eligible, and otherwise block on quit, the newWork signal, or a 50 millisecond ticker that re-checks for queues newly able to take a worker.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Popping a job must decrement the total job count and refresh the metric gauges; when the popped queue becomes empty the manager must delete the queue and its index entry, leave the worker count in place because workers may still be finishing earlier jobs, correct lastQueueAccessed for continued round-robining, and log a warning and return unchanged when the index is out of bounds.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package test utilities must build a testJob that delegates Execute to its ex function with its id and OnFailure to its onFail function, require both functions to be non-nil via newTestJob, and GetNumWorkers must read the underlying worker pool's numWorkers for assertions.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Decrementing a queue's worker count must delete the worker tracking entry once the queue no longer exists and the count has dropped below one, and re-adding a queue must preserve an existing non-zero worker count rather than resetting it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SimpleJob must adapt a bare func() to the Job interface: Execute calls the function and returns nil, and OnFailure panics with a message stating that SimpleJob cannot fail, since a SimpleJob never yields an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A Job must expose Execute, which performs the work synchronously when a cleanup function is supplied, and OnFailure, which handles the error Execute returned; the worker pool calls Execute and, only on a non-nil error, calls OnFailure(err) before invoking the job's cleanup function.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The behavior of Flag.String and Flag.Set is covered by tests in flag_test.go, including the parse of well formed key=value arguments and the rejection of arguments with no '=' character.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag and its String and Set methods together satisfy the standard library flag.Value interface, so the type can be registered directly with a flag set; String supplies the interface's display form and Set supplies its parsing form.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag is a map from string to string; it is used as the value type for a CLI flag so that each occurrence of the flag contributes one key and one value to the same map, and callers read the collected pairs straight out of that map.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag.Set parses one raw flag argument by cutting it at the first '=' character; the text before that separator becomes the key and the text after it, including any further '=' characters, becomes the value, and the pair is written into the map so a later argument with the same key overwrites the earlier value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag.String returns an empty string, because the collected key/value pairs are not rendered back into a flag string.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag.Set tolerates a nil receiver and allocates the underlying map on first use, so a Flag variable can be declared without initialization and still accept its first key=value argument.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Flag.Set returns an error that quotes the raw argument and reads "no '=' value in arg: %q" when the argument contains no '=' character, and in that case leaves the map unchanged.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package's behaviour should stay covered by the accompanying test file, which exercises the flag slice helper alongside the implementation.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both String and Set must be declared on a pointer receiver to StringFlag, so appending in Set mutates the caller's slice and the type satisfies the flag.Value interface when registered by address.

label: SpecRequirement
text: StringFlag.Set must append the received value to the slice through the pointer receiver, so successive calls grow the collection instead of overwriting the previous entry, and it must return a nil error on every call because no input is rejected.

label: SpecRequirement
text: StringFlag must be defined as a named type whose underlying type is a slice of strings, so a repeated flag accumulates an ordered list of the values passed on the command line rather than a single value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: StringFlag.String must return the elements of the slice joined with a single comma and no surrounding spaces, giving the flag package a stable textual rendering of the accumulated values.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Generating a forwarded request from a server-parsed http.Request and then parsing it back MUST yield a request identical in Method, RemoteAddr, Host, URL (deep equality), Header (deep equality) and body bytes; this equality is what util_test.go asserts and any change to either conversion function must keep it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: GenerateForwardedRequest MUST read the whole body of the incoming *http.Request and copy its method, host, remote address, the URL split into Scheme, Opaque, Host, Path, RawPath, RawQuery and Fragment, and each header key mapped to a HeaderEntry holding that key's values into a new Request; it MUST return the body read error rather than a partial Request when io.ReadAll fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NewRPCResponseWriter MUST return an initialized RPCResponseWriter with a live http.Header, an empty bytes.Buffer body, and a status code defaulting to 200, so a handler that never calls WriteHeader still reports success.

label: SpecRequirement
text: RPCResponseWriter MUST satisfy http.ResponseWriter while buffering instead of writing to a socket: Header returns the mutable header map, Write appends to the internal buffer and returns len(buf) with a nil error, WriteHeader records the given code, and StatusCode and Body expose the recorded status and buffered body so the response can be serialized into a Response message.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every field getter MUST tolerate a nil receiver, returning the field when the receiver is non-nil and the zero value otherwise: empty string for Method, Host, RemoteAddr and the URL and HeaderEntry string fields, a nil *URL, nil header-entry maps, nil byte slices, zero for StatusCode and LastRemoteWal, so callers can read a possibly-absent message without a nil check.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Request, URL, HeaderEntry and Response MUST each be a protobuf message: Reset MUST zero the receiver and store its message info, String MUST return the protobuf text form, ProtoMessage MUST be present, ProtoReflect MUST return a protoreflect.Message, and Descriptor MUST return the raw descriptor bytes and index path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: bufCloser MUST implement io.Closer over an embedded *bytes.Buffer, with Close resetting the buffer and returning a nil error, so a forwarded body can be closed by net/http without an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Response MUST carry the handler result across RPC as a status code, a body byte slice, a map of header name to HeaderEntry, and a last-remote-WAL counter, mirroring Request's method/url/header/body/host/remote-addr shape so both directions of the proxy share one encoding.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When the source request has TLS peer certificates, GenerateForwardedRequest MUST store each certificate's raw DER bytes, and only when that list is non-empty; ParseForwardedRequest MUST reverse this by calling x509.ParseCertificate on each entry into a tls.ConnectionState, returning an error if any certificate fails to parse.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParseForwardedRequest MUST rebuild an *http.Request from a Request, wrapping the carried body bytes in a seekable reader (the body must be re-readable), reassembling the URL from the same seven fields, expanding HeaderEntries back into a net/http header map, and returning an error when the seekable reader or TLS certificate parsing fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Expand() replace a leading `~` in the path with the home directory returned by Dir() and join it with the remainder using filepath.Join.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Dir() cache the first successful home directory in a package-level variable and return that cached value on subsequent calls without repeating discovery.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Dir() return an empty string together with the discovery error when the underlying OS-specific routine fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Expand() return the input path unchanged, with no error, when the path is empty or does not begin with `~`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Dir() hold the package cache lock around the cache check and the discovery call so concurrent callers cannot race on the cached value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Expand() return an empty string and propagate the error from Dir() when home directory discovery fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package's behaviour for Dir() and Expand() stay covered by the unit tests in homedir_test.go.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Expand() return an error with the text "cannot expand user-specific home directory" when the path begins with `~` followed by a character other than `/` or `\`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Dir() return the home directory of the executing user, choosing the discovery routine by operating system: dirWindows on windows and dirUnix on every other OS.

label: SpecRequirement
text: HostInfo, HostInfoStat, and VirtualMemoryStat must keep the JSON struct tags recorded on their fields (timestamp, cpu, cpu_times, disk, host, memory, and the per-metric tags such as total, available, used, usedPercent, free) so the collected host information serializes with stable key names.

label: SpecRequirement
text: hostinfo_test.go must exercise CollectHostInfo so the collection path, including its error aggregation, is covered by the package tests.

label: SpecInterface
name: HostInfo
signature: type HostInfo struct { Timestamp time.Time; CPU []cpu.InfoStat; CPUTimes []cpu.TimesStat; Disk []*disk.UsageStat; Host *HostInfoStat; Memory *VirtualMemoryStat }

label: SpecInterface
name: VirtualMemoryStat
signature: type VirtualMemoryStat struct { Total uint64; Available uint64; Used uint64; UsedPercent float64; Free uint64; Active uint64; Inactive uint64; Wired uint64; Laundry uint64; Buffers uint64; Cached uint64; Writeback uint64; Dirty uint64; WritebackTmp uint64; Shared uint64; Slab uint64; SReclaimable uint64; SUnreclaim uint64; PageTables uint64; SwapCached uint64; CommitLimit uint64; CommittedAS uint64; HighTotal uint64; HighFree uint64; LowTotal uint64; LowFree uint64; SwapTotal uint64; SwapFree uint64; Mapped uint64; VMallocTotal uint64; VMallocUsed uint64; VMallocChunk uint64; HugePagesTotal uint64; HugePagesFree uint64; HugePageSize uint64 }

label: SpecRequirement
text: CollectHostInfo must build a HostInfo stamped with the current time in UTC and fill its Host, Memory, Disk, CPU, and CPUTimes fields by calling CollectHostInfoStat, CollectHostMemory, disk.PartitionsWithContext, cpu.InfoWithContext, and cpu.TimesWithContext respectively. A failure in any one source must not abort the others: the failure is appended to a multierror wrapped in a HostInfoError labelled with the category name ("host", "memory", "disk", "cpu", "cpu_times"), the corresponding field is left unset, and the partially filled HostInfo is still returned alongside the aggregated error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: On OpenBSD the package must compile against a platform-specific file that replaces CollectHostInfo and CollectHostMemory with stubs returning a nil result and the error "host info not supported on this platform", so the unsupported platform still satisfies the same exported signatures.

label: SpecInterface
name: HostInfoError
signature: type HostInfoError struct { Type string; Err error }

label: SpecRequirement
text: HostInfoError must carry a Type naming the category that failed together with the wrapped Err, implement the error interface so Error() reports the failure, and implement WrappedErrors returning the wrapped error as a single-element slice so hashcorp/go-multierror can unwrap it when the aggregated error is printed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: CollectHostInfoStat must be exported as the standalone entry point that returns a HostInfoStat describing the general host, so callers that need only host metadata can obtain it without running the full collection.

label: SpecRequirement
text: CollectHostMemory must read virtual memory through mem.VirtualMemoryWithContext and return a VirtualMemoryStat populated field by field from the gopsutil result, including total, available, used, used percent, free, the BSD active/inactive/wired/laundry values, the Linux buffer/cache/slab/swap/hugepage values, and commit limits. It must return the underlying error unchanged with a nil result when the read fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When collecting disk usage, CollectHostInfo must enumerate partitions, then query usage per mountpoint, skipping a partition whose usage query fails and recording that failure under a HostInfoError labelled "disk.<index>" so the remaining partitions still contribute to the returned Disk slice.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The LocalAliases message must exist as a protobuf message holding a slice of Aliases reachable through GetAliases, used to carry the aliases scoped to a namespace as a single serializable record.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Entity message must expose generated getters for Aliases, ID, Name, Metadata, CreationTime, LastUpdateTime, MergedEntityIDs, Policies, BucketKey, MFASecrets, Disabled and NamespaceID, returning zero values for a nil receiver, so the store can reconstruct an entity together with its alias list, its merge history and its MFA configuration.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Group message must expose generated getters for ID, Name, Policies, ParentGroupIDs, MemberEntityIDs, Metadata, CreationTime, LastUpdateTime, ModifyIndex, BucketKey, Alias, Type and NamespaceID, each returning the zero value when the receiver is nil, so policy and storage code can read group relationships without a nil check.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ToSDKEntity must return nil for a nil input; otherwise it must allocate an alias slice of the same length as the entity's Aliases and convert every element through ToSDKAlias, copy Metadata into a new map, and carry ID, Name, Disabled, Aliases and NamespaceID onto the resulting logical.Entity.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Entity.SentinelKeys, Alias.SentinelKeys and Group.SentinelKeys must each return the set of field names that the matching SentinelGet accepts, so policy authors can enumerate the readable surface of the record and the two methods stay in agreement.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Clone must return a value independent of the receiver, produced by marshaling the message with proto.Marshal and unmarshaling the bytes into a fresh local value, so callers can mutate the copy without touching the original. A marshal failure must return an error of the form "failed to marshal group/entity/alias: %w" and an unmarshal failure "failed to unmarshal group/entity/alias: %w", each wrapping the underlying error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: EntityStorageEntry must expose getters for Personas, ID, Name, Metadata, CreationTime, LastUpdateTime, MergedEntityIDs, Policies, BucketKeyHash and MFASecrets, and each PersonaIndexEntry must expose getters for ID, EntityID, MountType, MountAccessor, MountPath, Metadata, Name, CreationTime, LastUpdateTime and MergedFromEntityIDs, so the persisted storage record retains its persona index and the mount-scoped fields needed to look an entity up from a login mount.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ToSDKAlias must return nil for a nil input, and otherwise build a logical.Alias carrying Name, ID, MountAccessor, MountType, NamespaceID and CustomMetadata from the internal alias, with Metadata copied element by element into a newly allocated map of the same capacity so later mutation of the SDK value does not alias the internal map.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Group.Clone, Entity.Clone and Alias.Clone must return a nil result and a non-nil error when the receiver is nil, so callers that clone optional records never panic. Group.Clone returns the error "nil group" and Entity.Clone returns "nil entity".

label: SpecRequirement
text: ToSDKGroup must return nil for a nil input and otherwise project ID, Name, a copied Metadata map and NamespaceID onto a logical.Group; ToSDKGroups must return nil for a nil input slice and otherwise allocate a slice of the same length and map each element through ToSDKGroup in order, so index correspondence with the input is preserved.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Alias message must expose generated getters for ID, CanonicalID, MountType, MountAccessor, MountPath, Metadata, Name, CreationTime, LastUpdateTime, MergedFromCanonicalIDs, NamespaceID, CustomMetadata, Local and LocalBucketKey, returning zero values for a nil receiver, covering both the mount binding and the local-alias bookkeeping a login alias needs.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Group, LocalAliases, Entity, Alias, EntityStorageEntry and PersonaIndexEntry must each implement the protobuf message contract: Reset to clear the message to its zero state, String for a textual rendering, ProtoMessage as the marker method, ProtoReflect returning a protoreflect.Message, and Descriptor returning the compressed file descriptor bytes and the message's index path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Entity.SentinelGet, Alias.SentinelGet and Group.SentinelGet must return the field value for a supported key and report an unrecognized key as an error rather than falling through with a nil value and no error, so policy evaluation never silently reads a missing field as nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Entity.UpsertAlias must walk the Aliases slice and, at the first index whose alias ID equals the given alias ID, overwrite that slot and return, preserving the alias's position; when no ID matches it must append the alias to the end of the slice. A nil alias argument must not be treated as a match.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Config must carry the identifying scalars Type, Name, ID, MountAccessor, UsernameFormat and NamespaceID, each with a generated getter that returns the field value. These getters must be usable on a nil receiver without panicking, returning the zero value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DuoConfig must hold the Duo credentials IntegrationKey and SecretKey together with APIHostname, PushInfo and the boolean UsePasscode, exposed through DuoConfig.GetIntegrationKey, GetSecretKey, GetAPIHostname, GetPushInfo and GetUsePasscode.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TOTPSecret must hold the per-user TOTP material Issuer, Period, Algorithm, Digits, Skew, KeySize, AccountName and Key, exposed through the matching getters on TOTPSecret. It repeats the TOTPConfig parameter set and adds AccountName and Key, so a stored secret is self-describing without a lookup of the parent method config.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PingIDConfig must hold the PingID settings UseBase64Key, UseSignature, Token, IDPURL, OrgAlias, AdminURL and AuthenticatorURL, exposed through the matching getters. UseSignature is boolean, the remaining fields are strings, and AuthenticatorURL is carried separately from IDPURL and AdminURL.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Config.SentinelKeys must return exactly the three key names "type", "name" and "mount_accessor", and Config.SentinelGet must resolve each of those keys to the Config field of the same meaning (Type, Name, MountAccessor). Any other key, and a nil receiver, must yield a nil value with a nil error rather than an error or a panic.

label: SpecRequirement
text: MFAEnforcementConfig must describe one enforcement rule through Name, NamespaceID, ID, the repeated lists MFAMethodIDs, AuthMethodAccessors, AuthMethodTypes, IdentityGroupIds and IdentityEntityIDs, each reachable through its getter. The rule therefore combines required methods with selector lists over auth mounts, auth types, identity groups and identity entities.

label: SpecRequirement
text: MFAEnforcementConfig.Clone must apply the same protobuf marshal/unmarshal round trip to produce an independent copy of an enforcement rule, returning the error "nil config" for a nil receiver and wrapping marshal and unmarshal failures with the same two messages used by Config.Clone.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Secret must carry a MethodName plus a Secret_Value oneof that currently admits only TOTPSecret. Secret.GetValue must return the set variant, Secret.GetTOTPSecret must return the TOTPSecret when that variant is set and nil otherwise, and Secret.GetMethodName must return the method name.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every message type in the package (Config, TOTPConfig, DuoConfig, OktaConfig, PingIDConfig, Secret, TOTPSecret, MFAEnforcementConfig) must satisfy the proto.Message contract: Reset must zero the receiver back to a fresh empty message, String must render the message text, ProtoMessage must exist as the marker method, ProtoReflect must return the message reflection view, and Descriptor must return the file descriptor bytes and message index.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TOTPConfig must hold the TOTP parameters of an MFA method: Issuer, Period, Algorithm, Digits, Skew, KeySize, QRSize and MaxValidationAttempts, exposed through GetIssuer, GetPeriod, GetAlgorithm, GetDigits, GetSkew, GetKeySize, GetQRSize and GetMaxValidationAttempts. Numeric parameters (Period, Skew, KeySize, MaxValidationAttempts) are unsigned 32-bit, while Algorithm, Digits and QRSize are signed 32-bit, so algorithm and digit selection are carried as enums.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Config must be a protobuf message whose Config_Config oneof holds at most one provider configuration, chosen from TOTPConfig, OktaConfig, DuoConfig and PingIDConfig. Config.GetConfig must return the set variant, and each typed accessor (GetTOTPConfig, GetOktaConfig, GetDuoConfig, GetPingIDConfig) must return the variant when it is that type and nil when another variant is set.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Config.Clone must return an independent copy of the receiver produced by marshaling the receiver to protobuf and unmarshaling into a new Config, so mutating the clone never mutates the original. A nil receiver must return an error whose text is "nil config" rather than panic. Marshal and unmarshal failures must be wrapped with the messages "failed to marshal config" and "failed to unmarshal config" respectively.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OktaConfig must hold the Okta credentials OrgName and APIToken together with the Production and PrimaryEmail booleans and the BaseURL override, exposed through OktaConfig.GetOrgName, GetAPIToken, GetProduction, GetBaseURL and GetPrimaryEmail.

It isolates the harness boilerplate — flag parsing, TLS provider derivation, and multiplexed serving — from the backend implementation, which lives in the parent `approle` package and is reached only through the `approle.Factory` symbol. Keeping this file thin means the backend stays testable and buildable without the plugin harness, while the binary itself remains compileable against host versions that predate plugin AutoMTLS.

This package centralizes the image selection, the readiness probe, and the connection string format, and it allows CI environments that already provide a MySQL server to short-circuit container startup through the MYSQL_URL environment variable. Keeping the mapping in a checked-in YAML file makes the cluster topology reproducible across machines instead of relying on manual kind flags.

intent: This context exists to pin down the deploy/examples/atproto/market example as an executable specification of what the kcp deno runtime must support: peer services that reach each other only by cluster-local name over TLS, with identity and certificates supplied from outside the pod, and a market bidder that reaches those same peers the same way. It is the reference topology that exercises workspace creation, per-workspace API bindings, per-workspace RBAC, per-workspace OpenBao certificate authority selection, the provider's virtual DNS table and shim, and the TLS leaf injection path, and it exists so that a regression in any of those surfaces shows up as a failing verifier pod rather than as an untested assumption in the provider. The example carries its own live acceptance, accept.sh, so that it is proven by bringing the whole topology up and reaching it, not only by decoding its manifests and fitting them to the schemas.

Keeping these as standalone YAML files under integrationtest/vault lets the test harness apply them verbatim to a throwaway cluster, isolating the test from any pre-existing RBAC state.

name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-stubbolt

intent: This context exists because the KV secrets engine must be runnable as an out-of-process OpenBao plugin, not only as an in-tree backend. Its purpose is to adapt the kv backend's factory to the plugin serving protocol: it collects the TLS material the plugin needs to talk back to the OpenBao server, converts it into the provider function the plugin SDK expects, and starts the plugin server with the KV factory registered as the backend. It is deliberately thin, holding no KV logic and no policy of its own; all storage behavior lives in the kv package it references.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-kv-cmd-kv

intent: This context exists to specify a test double for the agent proxy sink abstraction. Callers that must not touch a real destination (file or network) can construct a mock sink through NewSink, hand it to code that expects sink.Sink, drive token writes through the interface, and then read back the last token with Token to assert what was written. It is pure test scaffolding: no persistence, no error paths, no external side effects.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agentproxyshared-sink-mock

intent: This context exists so the PKI extension package can turn a stream of docker container log output into per-line callbacks during tests. The container log writer in this package duplicates the LogConsumerWriter type that also exists in the sdk/helper/docker and sdk/helper/testcluster/docker packages, differing only in that its callback field is exported as Consumer rather than unexported. The context documents that helper and the test files that depend on the pkiext package's test scaffolding, so that changes to log handling or to the pkiext test helpers keep the observed behaviour intact.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-pkiext

intent: This context exists to record that third_party/openbao/.github/ is vendored upstream configuration, not deno-kcp project logic. It fixes the boundary between the OpenBao subtree's own actionlint, dependabot, and security-insights settings and the parent repository's workflow, dependency, and security configuration, so that a reader or a tool does not mistake the vendored YAML for first-party deno-kcp policy. It also records that the directory exports nothing callable, which keeps the low-confidence OpenBao symbol matches in internal/provider from being read as consumers of these files.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-github

intent: The context exists so the agent exec server's contract is described independently of the surrounding OpenBao agent: which configuration the server accepts, how it derives runner state from environment templates, under what conditions it restarts or stops the child process, what it returns on cancellation, template error and child exit, and how restart-on-secret-changes values are interpreted. It documents the boundary between the template-render path (incoming token and rendered events) and the process-supervision path so a reader can reason about restart, debounce and shutdown behavior without reading the whole agent command tree.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agent-exec

intent: This context exists to pin down the contract of the cert plugin's binary entry point: the sequence of flag parsing, TLS material derivation from the plugin API client meta, and the multiplexed serve call that registers `cert.Factory` as the backend factory. It matters because the entry point is the boundary between the plugin process and the OpenBao/Vault plugin protocol, and because the explicit `TLSProviderFunc` is what keeps the plugin loadable by older Vault versions without AutoMTLS. It also fixes the failure behavior — log and exit non-zero — so a failed serve is never silently ignored. The context deliberately holds no business logic: everything about certificate auth lives in the cert package, and this file must stay a thin bootstrapper.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-cert-cmd-cert

intent: This context exists to describe the vendored OpenBao AppRole auth-method package that deno-kcp carries under `third_party/openbao`, so its public surface (constructor, functional options, `Login`) and its documented behavior (single secret-ID source, late resolution of file and environment values, bounded file read, optional wrapping-token unwrap, write to `auth/<mountPath>/login`) are recorded as requirements rather than re-derived from source on each change. It anchors the contract other parts of the repository rely on when authenticating to OpenBao with a role ID and secret ID, and it marks the package as upstream code whose behavior is already exercised by its own tests.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-api-auth-approle

intent: This context exists so the MySQL database backend can be shipped and executed as a separate process that OpenBao talks to over the dbplugin RPC protocol. The main.go entrypoint isolates only the composition step: construct the MySQL plugin with the standard (non-legacy) username template and register it with ServeMultiplex. Keeping this as its own binary lets the MySQL engine be built, versioned, and mounted independently of the OpenBao server binary, with the legacy username template variant living in a sibling plugin directory.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-mysql-mysql-database-plugin

intent: This context exists so the agent proxy can run as a native Windows service. The Windows service manager drives the process through a handler interface, but the rest of the agent only needs one portable signal: a channel that fires when the service controller asks the process to stop. ShutdownChannel is that portable surface, and serviceWindows.Execute is the adapter that translates Windows service control requests into it. The init hook keeps normal interactive invocations unaffected, registering the handler only in a real service session.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agentproxyshared-winsvc

intent: This context exists to describe the standalone, self-contained main package that OpenBao builds into the influxdb-database-plugin binary. It matters because the plugin is compiled and shipped as a separate process that OpenBao's database secrets engine launches and talks to over the dbplugin RPC interface; the entry point is the entire build target. Knowing that Run is a thin wrapper over dbplugin.ServeMultiplex(influxdb.New) fixes the contract: the plugin has no configuration of its own at startup, no flags, and no error paths, and all InfluxDB-specific behavior (connection handling, credential templating, user lifecycle) lives in the imported influxdb package rather than here.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-influxdb-influxdb-database-plugin

intent: This context exists so command entrypoints across OpenBao can accept PGP recipients uniformly: operators name key files or keybase users on the command line, the package resolves them to entities, encrypts each share to its recipient, and reports fingerprints that operators verify out of band. It is a third-party vendored dependency under third_party/openbao, described so the surrounding repository can reason about its contract without re-reading the upstream source.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-pgpkeys

intent: This context exists so the userpass credential backend can be run as a separate process under OpenBao's plugin multiplexing protocol, which is how a plugin binary is launched and handed a listener and TLS material by the host. It is the process boundary: everything about the backend's behavior is elsewhere, but the backend cannot be loaded at all without this main package parsing the plugin API client flags, constructing the TLS provider function that keeps backwards compatibility with hosts lacking plugin AutoMTLS, and serving userpass.Factory over multiplex. The error path exists so a failure to serve is reported and turned into a nonzero exit rather than a silent hang.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-userpass-cmd-userpass

intent: The context exists to specify the Transit logical backend that the repository vendors from OpenBao: what the plugin factory must construct, how the policy cache is sized from storage, how policies are fetched under locks, how the external key factory bridges to the system view, and which Transit API paths and batch request/response shapes the backend must serve. It gives the contract for the transit package so that consumers and refactors can rely on the exported entry points and the path surface without re-reading every file.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-transit

intent: The context exists to specify the Kubernetes auth method client helper so that callers and reimplementations know the exact constructor contract, option semantics, error strings, and login entry point. It pins down which behaviors are required of NewKubernetesAuth and of each LoginOption so that the Kubernetes backend login can be constructed and exercised against an *api.Client without reading the source. It also records that LoginOption here is a per-package type, not shared with the approle, ldap, or userpass packages.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-api-auth-kubernetes

intent: This context exists to give integration tests of the Kubernetes auth backend a way to talk to a Vault/OpenBao instance that runs inside a Kubernetes pod. Because the container is not reachable directly from the test host, the package provides the two primitives the tests need: an authenticated clientset built from a caller-named kubeconfig context, and a port-forward that exposes the pod's Vault port 8200 on a free local port, together with a close function so the tunnel can be torn down. Both helpers share the same kubeconfig resolution path, and every failure is returned as a wrapped error naming the step that failed, so a broken test setup reports where it broke.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest-k8s

intent: This context is the trigger decider, the piece of the deno-kcp control plane that turns a finished policy workflow run into a deno job. It exists so the RunTrigger reconciliation decision is testable and side-effect free: the reconciler decides, and the provider layer acts. When the referenced run succeeds and its outputs match the trigger's match map, the decider asks for a job named <trigger>-<run> and records the run as consumed so the same run never fires twice; cancelled, failed, or unfinished runs leave the trigger pending or skipped. Deletion is handled by asking for finalizer removal.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-trigger

intent: This context exists to stand up a disposable, reproducible Valkey instance for the OpenBao internal builtin database/valkey plugin tests, and to publish the connection settings those tests read from the environment. Terraform owns the lifecycle: apply starts the container and regenerates the environment file, destroy tears the container down, so the test fixture is created and removed by the same tooling that runs everything else.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-valkey-bootstrap-terraform

intent: This context exists so the DenoPod lifecycle can be specified and tested without a Kubernetes client or a live deno process. Reconcile is the single decision point that turns an observed pod plus its execution observation into a target state, and every branch is covered by internal/denopod/denopod_test.go, which drives the reconciler with table-style Observed values and asserts on the returned Result. The package mirrors the shape of internal/policyengine but adds exit-code and output capture, so the spec records the exact contract other reconcile loops in this repository follow.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-denopod

intent: The context exists to specify the Cassandra database plugin of the embedded OpenBao distribution that deno-kcp vendors: a secrets engine that dynamically provisions, rotates, and revokes Cassandra users on behalf of the platform. It is third-party code carried in-tree rather than written here, so the spec records the contract the vendored copy must satisfy (the dbplugin method set, the gocql session lifecycle, CQL statement splitting and interpolation, and rollback on failed creation) for anyone reading, testing, or modifying it.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-cassandra

intent: This context exists to pin the behaviour of the vendored OpenBao userpass auth method as this repository consumes it: the constructor contract, the mount-path option, the deferred password read, and the validate rules. It captures the code that is there so changes to the vendored copy can be checked against the expected interface and error strings, and so the conformance to api.AuthMethod is recorded.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-api-auth-userpass

intent: This context exists to mark the boundary of the vendored upstream OpenBao tree inside deno-kcp, so that readers and tools do not confuse it with deno-kcp's first-party OpenBao handling in internal/provider. It records that the copies under third_party/openbao are upstream sources carried alongside the repository, together with the two golangci-lint configurations and the publiccode.yml that travel with them, and it records that the tree exposes no interfaces of its own to the deno-kcp module. It is a containment and provenance note rather than a behavioral contract: the renames and edits to make upstream OpenBao usable by deno-kcp happen in the first-party packages, not here.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao

intent: This context exists to hold the one test package that proves deno-kcp works against real infrastructure and against the checked-in examples. It separates what can be verified from the repository alone (offline_test.go, examples.go) from what needs a running kcp, kine, deno and policy-engine (live_test.go, fixture_test.go) from what additionally needs the pinned OpenBao (bao_test.go, openbao_live_test.go), so the cheap checks run everywhere and the expensive ones are gated behind explicit opt-in. The fixture layer exists so that every live test describes intent in terms of typed Kubernetes objects and named expectations rather than raw HTTP, and so the OpenBao version certificates are issued by is the one the repository pins, never whatever binary happens to be on PATH. The example registry covers every kcp-kind manifest the repository ships, including the atproto market manifests under deploy/examples/atproto/market, so the offline tier decodes and schema-fits them with no cluster.
label: SpecContext
name: test-integration

intent: This context exists so the builtin plugin registry's lookup surface can be described and depended on without reading the vendored OpenBao sources: it is the single place that maps a builtin plugin name plus plugin type to its factory, its deprecation status, and the list of names that are still considered builtin. It exists because the rest of the tree, notably Vault core, binds to a BuiltinRegistry interface offering exactly Get, Keys, Contains and DeprecationStatus, so the behaviour of those four methods, including what happens for an unknown name or an unrecognised plugin type, is the contract callers rely on.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-builtinplugins

intent: This context exists because streaming server logs over the API needs a fan-out point that can be attached and detached from a live logger without changing the logger's own level, and that must not let a slow consumer stall the logging path. It is the mechanism behind the sys/monitor endpoint and the monitor CLI command: the caller constructs a Monitor with a buffer size and logger options, calls Start to obtain the message channel, reads from it, and calls Stop to detach. It also bounds how much is lost when the reader lags, by dropping overflow writes and reporting the dropped count rather than blocking.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-monitor

intent: This context exists to record the vendored GitHub issue-template metadata that deno-kcp carries for the OpenBao third-party tree. It is declarative configuration, not code: the three YAML files shape how contributors file documentation/ecosystem reports and RFC proposals against the upstream project, and config.yml decides which contact links the issue chooser offers. The context is documented so that its contents are known to be upstream-owned metadata with no Go build surface, letting future changes be treated as upstream syncs rather than local behaviour changes.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-github-issue-template

intent: This context exists so that callers that must refuse to read secrets from world- or group-writable files, or that must confirm a file is owned by a specific uid, have one audited place to ask. It separates the checks that are meaningful everywhere (mode-bit inspection, digesting, permission comparison) from the ones that need POSIX uid/gid data (fileinfo_unix.go) and the stubs that keep Windows builds compiling, so a security check written once behaves the same wherever it is called.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-osutil

intent: Provide the PostgreSQL database engine with correct SCRAM verifier generation so generated role passwords are stored by the server in the salted-challenge form PostgreSQL validates. It exists as a small, self-contained third-party package under internal/builtin/database/postgresql/scram/, keeping the hashing primitive separate from the engine's connection and role management logic and testable in isolation through scram_test.go.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-postgresql-scram

intent: This context exists so the specification records the key=value flag helper that OpenBao's command layer uses to let users pass repeatable key=value options on the CLI, pinning down exactly how a raw argument is parsed into the map and what happens on malformed input, so that a reimplementation or a port preserves the same parsing contract, the same error string, and the same lazy nil-map allocation.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-flag-kv

intent: The package exists so OpenBao can describe a request/response profile in HCL and evaluate it with pluggable data sources. The CEL source exposes `requests`, `responses` and `input` variables only when the matching source is present, so a profile can reference request and response data without failing at compile time when that data is unavailable. The engine evaluates the profile against a recorded `EvaluationHistory`, produces a `logical.Response`, and can dump a debug map. Sources are decoupled behind the `Source` interface, so each backend (CEL expression, template, environment variable, file, request, response, plugin input) is registered by name and built lazily.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-profiles

intent: This context exists because the OpenBao server, agent, and proxy commands need to tell systemd that the process has finished starting up, and the vendored helper provides that capability in-tree. Keeping the sd_notify logic in its own package means the command layer only needs to call Notify with a state string such as "READY=1", and the helper decides from NOTIFY_SOCKET whether a systemd supervisor is actually present. It is a third-party vendored component inside this repository, so its behavior must keep matching upstream.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-systemd

intent: This context exists so the agent proxy cache can survive restarts. It gives the lease cache a disk-backed persistent storage layer whose contents are encrypted at rest and whose schema can be upgraded in place. It is the bolt-backed implementation of the persistent cache contract, keeping leases ordered so parents are restored before children and keeping the latest auto-auth and retrieval tokens available for restore.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agentproxyshared-cache-cacheboltdb

intent: The context exists to pin down the contract of the two exported helpers in third_party/openbao/internal/helper/template/template.go, which is the only place in the tree that fixes the variable names a path-filtering template may reference. It exists because the filtering templates are authored as strings elsewhere (from configuration or request input) and must be compiled and evaluated with a stable, agreed-upon data shape; anyone changing that data shape, the constructor used for compilation, or the error propagation would break every caller that writes a filter template.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-template

intent: This context exists so tests written against the standard testing.TB surface, including calls to Parallel, can be handed to interfaces that require testinginterface.T. It bridges the two testing abstractions without rewriting the calling tests, and deliberately neutralizes parallelism at that boundary.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-benchhelpers

intent: This context exists to hold the provider-side controller logic of deno-kcp as a single describable unit: the reconcile engines and their per-kind reconcile files, the Reader/Runtime/TokenMinter port interfaces the engines depend on, the Registry implementation that satisfies those ports against Kubernetes, the admission adapter that gates runs by capacity, the informer-backed watch cache, and the metrics surface. It is the boundary between the queue/reconcile library code and the concrete cluster API, so the spec here fixes which ports exist, what each method must do, and which invariants (default concurrency policy, finalizer removal, cache-served reads, cluster path resolution) must hold.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-provider

intent: This context exists to pin down the executable entrypoint that registers the PostgreSQL database plugin with OpenBao's dbplugin RPC layer. It is a packaging and wiring artifact, not behavior: its whole job is to hand a constructor, postgresql.New, to dbplugin.ServeMultiplex so the plugin binary can be spawned as a separate process and satisfy the dbplugin.Database interface (Initialize, NewUser, UpdateUser, DeleteUser, Type, Close). Anyone asking where the PostgreSQL database plugin process starts, or which constructor a build must link, gets that answer here.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-postgresql-postgresql-database-plugin

intent: The context exists to describe the host information collection helper that Vault/OpenBao diagnostics rely on to report the machine environment. It exists so that a reader or a regenerator knows exactly which entry points the package exports, what each one returns, how collection failures are represented and accumulated, and how the package degrades on unsupported platforms, without having to re-read the vendored third-party source.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-hostutil

intent: These are test-fixture manifests, not application code: they exist so the kubernetes secrets-engine integration tests have a real cluster with known ServiceAccounts, known RBAC grants, and a host-reachable Vault. The split is deliberate — hostPortPatch is applied over the Vault helm chart, testServiceAccounts creates the subjects, testRoles declares the permissions, and testBindings attaches them, so a test can assert behaviour for a privileged ServiceAccount, an under-privileged one, and a token-creating one.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-kubernetes-integrationtest-vault

intent: Test code elsewhere in the OpenBao tree needs a real Cassandra instance to run against, without hand-writing container plumbing at each call site. This package exists to make that a two-line affair: call PrepareTestContainer with a handful of ContainerOpt values, get back a Host for dialing and a function to tear the container down. The option type keeps the container configuration extensible, so a test can override the container name, image, version, environment, copied-in files or TLS settings without the helper growing a wide parameter list.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-testhelpers-cassandra

intent: This context specifies the template-rendering server that the OpenBao agent uses to run the internal Consul Template runner: it accepts the agent's template configurations and an incoming Vault token channel, restarts the runner when a new token arrives, retries with backoff on runner errors, and terminates early once all templates are rendered when exit-after-auth is configured. The spec records the construction, configuration surface and lifecycle guarantees of that server so the behaviour can be preserved.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agent-template

intent: This context exists so the deno-kcp repository keeps a describable, self-contained picture of the OpenBao logging helper it vendors under third_party. It records the observable behavior of the rotating file writer and of the log level/format parsing and logger setup helpers, so changes to that vendored code can be reviewed against a stated contract instead of re-reading the sources each time. It is a reference context, not a feature: nothing here is authored by this repository, and the requirements below describe what the vendored code already does.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-logging

intent: This context exists so the vendored Valkey database plugin can be read, reviewed and modified without opening the whole OpenBao third_party tree. It covers the connection producer that owns config parsing, TLS material and the radix client pool, and the ValkeyDB plugin surface that the database secrets engine drives for user creation, update and deletion. Pinning the producer's validation order, the connection_url versus discrete-parameter exclusivity, the valkeys scheme shortcut and the lazy TLS pool construction gives a reader the exact contract the rest of the plugin depends on.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-valkey

intent: This context exists so tests across the OpenBao tree can mint certificates without hand-rolling crypto: a builder plus functional options gives one call site per test, with sensible expiry, key usage and CA/leaf defaults, and fatal test errors instead of returned errors. The spec records that option-modelled construction surface and the defaults NewCert applies so the helper can be reimplemented or consumed without guessing.
label: SpecContext
